event-handlers__valid__01.reason: TypeScript proves 'string' + some_func() is a string ('+' with a string operand always yields one), so the onLy value is provably never a listener; upstream's constant folder cannot fold past the call and stays silent.

jsx-no-undef__valid__05.reason: Upstream's typescriptEnabled tells the rule to stay silent because tsc will report TS2304 for the undefined component itself. This checker's certification must not depend on a separate tsc invocation being run and read, so it reports the undefined component regardless; the option is deliberately not carried.

no-array-handlers__valid__10.reason: SafeArray is undeclared in this corpus case, so the cast fails to resolve and TypeScript types the expression as the tuple itself, which the checker correctly reports as an array handler. In a real project the cast resolves to SafeArray<number> and the checker honours it, exactly as upstream intends.

no-destructure__valid__10.reason: Upstream's own comment says this is caught by solid/reactivity rather than by no-destructure; the checker reports it from the destructure rule instead of a second one.

reactivity__invalid__13.reason: This is upstream's analysis-integrity warning for a capture shape its syntax analyzer cannot follow, not a Solid runtime defect. The checker resolves sources through TypeScript symbols and does not expose analyzer bookkeeping as a user rule.

reactivity__invalid__14.reason: Keeping only a signal setter is valid Solid when a scope writes but never reads the value. Upstream reports the partial tuple because its syntax analyzer expects both slots; the checker follows the resolved setter contract.

reactivity__invalid__15.reason: As reactivity__invalid__13: this is an upstream analyzer-capture warning for a discarded createMemo result, not evidence of an incorrect reactive read/write contract.

reactivity__invalid__25.reason: SomeContext is undeclared in this corpus case, so neither TypeScript nor the compiler can prove a Context.Provider contract. The checker does not infer framework semantics from a property spelled Provider.

reactivity__invalid__26.reason: SomeProvider is undeclared and a component name ending in Provider is not proof that its value prop is eagerly consumed. The checker requires a resolved component or contract rather than upstream's name convention.

reactivity__invalid__32.reason: A tagged template hands its interpolations to the tag, which may legitimately call them, so uncalled-accessor deliberately excludes them; see its value_position doc.

reactivity__invalid__34.reason: Solid 1.x mapArray only allocates and returns an adapter; its list and mapper execute when that returned function is invoked. Here createCustomStore is never called, so canonical-symbol reachability and the AST call graph prove the mapper's store read is dormant.

reactivity__invalid__35.reason: Solid 1.x mapArray does not execute its mapper until the returned adapter is invoked. The adapter is assigned to result and never consumed, so the mapper's index-accessor read is unreachable and upstream's eager syntax report is a false positive.

reactivity__invalid__36.reason: Solid 1.x indexArray does not execute its mapper until the returned adapter is invoked. The adapter is assigned to result and never consumed, so the mapper's item-accessor read is unreachable and upstream's eager syntax report is a false positive.

reactivity__invalid__37.reason: Solid's compiler classifies a dynamic component property as CallerContext and lowers it to a lazy getter, so signal() is evaluated when the child reads the prop rather than once at the parent call site. Upstream's report contradicts that compiler fact.

reactivity__valid__23.reason: Solid 1.9's runWithOwner saves Listener and sets it to null while invoking the callback. Capturing the current owner inside an effect restores ownership, not dependency tracking, so the signal read is genuinely untracked and the checker intentionally reports it.

reactivity__valid__24.reason: runWithOwner(undefined, callback) clears Listener while the callback runs in no supplied owner. The checker follows the Solid 1.9 runtime and reports the signal read; upstream's valid case is a false negative.

reactivity__valid__51.reason: useSignal is unresolved in this corpus case. The checker does not infer a snapshot or tracking contract from use-prefixed spelling; an intentional initial props snapshot can be made explicit with untrack, or an imported helper can provide a package contract.
